rationale: I read the held original of EO 8875 (6 FR 4483, August 28, 1941) in full and confirmed identity; paragraphs 8, 10 and 11 are one-time acts, but paragraphs 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 and 9 are continuing delegations of priority and allocation powers and a continuing limitation. The basis texts do not end the order: EO 9024 (7 FR 329) para. 2(c) directs the War Production Board chairman to 'exercise the powers vested in the Supply Priorities and Allocations Board by Executive Order No. 8875', and para. 7 abolishes SPAB but says EO 8875 is 'hereby amended accordingly', superseding only conflicting provisions; EO 9040 (7 FR 527) abolishes OPM and transfers its functions and powers to the WPB chairman and rescinds EO 8629, not EO 8875. Abolition of agencies with transfer of their EO 8875 functions is an amendment and continuation, not an end (the OFR catalog itself records EO 9024 as 'Amends'), so under the owner's rule that an endpoint needs a reason, the held basis does not establish that EO 8875 ended; the later held EO 9638 (1945) carries WPB functions forward to the Civilian Production Administration without naming EO 8875, and no held source identifies its end, so status no is not shown through 2026-10-14. Every evidence record's held text was re-hashed against its recorded text_sha256 and every recorded span was compared with the held file (all matched); the producer's two history observations were checked against the held texts and no history flags require resolution.
